hba1c.fact: Sustained high blood glucose is associated with microvascular complications, including kidney complications. HbA1c is a measure of average glucose exposure, not a kidney-function test.
hba1c.source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026, Section 11

sbp.fact: Blood-pressure management is an important part of reducing kidney and cardiovascular risk in people with diabetes. A single blood-pressure reading does not diagnose chronic kidney disease.
sbp.source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026, Section 11

dbp.fact: Blood-pressure management is an important part of reducing kidney and cardiovascular risk in people with diabetes. A single blood-pressure reading does not diagnose chronic kidney disease.
dbp.source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026, Section 11

dm_duration_years.fact: Duration is useful clinical context: kidney disease may develop after years of diabetes, but it can also be present when type 2 diabetes is first diagnosed. Duration alone cannot establish kidney disease.
dm_duration_years.source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026, Section 11

bmi.fact: Weight management is part of comprehensive care for people with diabetes and kidney risk. BMI is a body-size measure and cannot diagnose kidney disease by itself.
bmi.source: KDIGO 2022 Diabetes Management in CKD Guideline

waist_cm.fact: Waist size is a measure of central body size, not a kidney test. Interpret its model contribution as an association in this dataset rather than proof of a cause.
waist_cm.source: Project methodology note: NHANES cross-sectional, non-causal attribution

insulin_use.fact: Insulin use records a treatment choice. By itself, it does not establish diabetes severity or the presence of kidney disease; interpretation depends on clinical context.
insulin_use.source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026, Section 9

diabetes_pills.fact: Use of diabetes pills reflects a treatment plan. Medication use alone cannot diagnose kidney disease or prove that treatment caused the model prediction.
diabetes_pills.source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026, Section 9

age.fact: Kidney-risk assessment uses kidney markers such as eGFR and urine albumin alongside a person’s broader clinical context. Age alone cannot establish kidney disease.
age.source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026, Section 11

hdl.fact: HDL cholesterol is a cardiometabolic measure, not a direct test for kidney disease. Its contribution here is a statistical association learned by this model.
hdl.source: Project methodology note: NHANES cross-sectional, non-causal attribution

total_chol.fact: Total cholesterol is a cardiometabolic measure, not a direct test for kidney disease. Its contribution here is a statistical association learned by this model.
total_chol.source: Project methodology note: NHANES cross-sectional, non-causal attribution

female.fact: Sex is a demographic model input. A SHAP contribution describes how this model used the variable in its training data; it does not mean sex itself caused the predicted result.
female.source: Project methodology note: NHANES cross-sectional, non-causal attribution

dm_diagnosed.fact: A reported clinician diagnosis is distinct from the HbA1c-based eligibility rule used to form this study cohort. This variable records reported diagnosis status, not kidney status.
dm_diagnosed.source: NHANES data documentation and project cohort definition
